title: A Glyph Is Not a Letter, a Token Is Not a Word, a Space Is Not a Space: What the Units of Voynichese Are Not
summary: This preprint compares Zandbergen–Landini EVA with matched prose, cipher and pseudotext controls using quire-level resampling. It measures the structure carried by adjacent glyphs, token identities, and graded separators and publishes the analysis code and data.
established: In the tested corpus, the preceding token identity explains 0.79% of capped token entropy after shuffle correction, while the last and first glyphs across adjacent tokens share 0.197 bits of shuffle-corrected mutual information.

Uncertain separators have higher cross-boundary cohesion and narrower image-coordinate gaps than certain separators. Coordinate gap width distinguished the two classes with AUC 0.905 in the matched sample, with the same direction in a small blind pixel audit.
Byte-pair merges identify an early multi-symbol scale of reduced adjacent dependence, with a minimum at 32 merges when scored on omitted quires and at 64 in the pooled fit.

The tested Naibbe and self-citation outputs approximate the manuscript's low glyph entropy, early merge scale, weak token order and null substitution-attack differential. Their tested outputs have substantially weaker edge-glyph dependence and fewer singleton types than the manuscript at matched token counts.

open.question: Can the graded separator distinction be reproduced with independently segmented image measurements at manuscript scale?
open.check: Measure ink-to-ink gap widths blind to the transcription labels, matching the neighboring glyph pair and accounting for page or quire clustering.

open.question: Can a candidate text-production procedure reproduce both the strong cross-token edge dependence and the singleton-rich vocabulary at the manuscript's sample size?
open.check: At matched token counts and with fixed generator settings, compare shuffle-corrected edge-glyph mutual information and singleton-type fraction jointly against the manuscript and the published controls.
